thread:
maria-g: Quick status — brought up delta9b-int4 canary (v0.1.3) against production-like traffic. Accuracy evals look within tolerance, but we're seeing intermittent OOMs when concurrency spikes.
devin: can you paste the error snippet?
maria-g: sure, here's the tail from the serving node:
```
2026-03-22 15:12:02.341 ERROR inference: worker-7 OOM while allocating KV cache for seq_len=1300, batch=12
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runtime/serve.py", line 412, in handle_request
    kv_cache.alloc(new_size)
  File "/srv/runtime/kv.py", line 89, in alloc
    raise OutOfMemoryError(detail)
OutOfMemoryError: requested 1.2GB, available 950MB
```
maria-g: pattern: spiky tails when some requests go to max_new_tokens ~1024 and microbatching packs them.
sanjay: Did we enable the int4 per-layer fallback? That makes the allocator a bit noisier.
leah: We shipped the layerwise type-mix heuristic in the canary (to maintain quality). Could be fragging the slab.
devin: two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) lower default max_new_tokens for this model to 256 for hosted runs, 2) enforce smaller microbatch cap (batch_size<=8) for the canary pool. Both quick to flip.
maria-g: agreed. Also thinking to add a soft-evict + reserve of 1GB for KV cache in the runtime config for this model so transient spikes don't OOM.
infra-ci: deploy-bot: Scheduled canary config change: set max_new_tokens=256, microbatch_max=8 on pool delta9b-int4-canary at 15:30 UTC. (runbook id: RB-ML-522)
deploy-bot: rolling change started
maria-g: after dropping max_new_tokens to 256 I re-ran the synthetic stress harness. No OOMs in 30m, latency P95 dropped ~18ms, quality delta negligible on our eval set.
sanjay: good. We should also add a targeted regression test: 50k prompt corpus with long-tail prompts (>=700 tokens) and ensure soft-evict behavior doesn't degrade perplexity >0.5 relative to float baseline.
leah: I'll add that to the model eval pipeline (eval-suite delta9b-int4 / longtail). Also proposing an adaptive path: if request requests >512 tokens and system load >70%, route to delta9b-int8 variant until load subsides.
devin: routing is easy via policy rule: if load>70% AND prompt_len>512 -> target=model:delta9b-int8:fallback. We should monitor cost impact though.
maria-g: notes for postmortem: root cause is memory fragmentation combined with layerwise mixed-precision allocation pattern. Int4 packing increased allocation churn and slab fragmentation under high concurrency.
sanjay: longer-term: look into a per-model allocator tuning: slab size bump for delta9b-int4 (e.g., 32MB->64MB), prefer guard reserve for KV and early compaction heuristics.
leah: I'll open a short RFC with measurements. For the immediate rollout: keep max_new_tokens=256 default for hosted and dedicated canaries, microbatch_max=8, enable soft-evict reserve 1GB. After 24h with stable metrics we can consider gradual bump.
maria-g: thanks — I'll monitor SLOs and quality dashboards. tagging infra for any followups.
infra-ci: created ticket ML-1159: "delta9b-int4 canary OOMs — paging allocator tuning and evals" with links to logs and the eval run.
devin: cute to add a short smoke script to the model bringup checklist to hit rare long prompts, I'll add a line.
maria-g: cool. If anyone wants to see the exact runtime knobs I toggled:
```
# snippet from canary override
{
  "model": "delta9b-int4",
  "overrides": {
    "defaults.max_new_tokens": 256,
    "batching.microbatch_max": 8,
    "runtime.kv_reserve_bytes": 1073741824,
    "fallback_policy": "route-to-delta9b-int8-on-high-load"
  }
}
```
leah: LGTM. we'll meet tomorrow 10:00 to review allocator metrics and decide slab bump.
maria-g: thanks all, closing the thread after monitoring window.
